102. Reasonable foreseeability means:
(A) Mere possibility
(B) Expectation of sensible person
(C) Foreseeability of probable consequences of his act by an average prudent
person
(D) Remote possibility of a particular consequence of his consequence by a reasonable
person
103. A renowned judgment in which reasonable foreseeability test was discussed by the
Privy Council, was:
(A) Scott v. Shephard
(B) Overseas Tankship UK Ltd. Morts Dock and Engineering Co. Ltd. (Wagon
v.
Mound Case)
(C) Donoghue v. Stevenson
(D) Re Polemis and Furness, Withy & Co
104. In which of the following judgment the neighbour principle was propounded?
(A) Scott v. Shephard
(B) Rylands v. Fletcher
(C) Donoghue v. Stevenson
(D) Overseas Tankship UK Ltd. Morts Dock and Engineering Co. Ltd. (Wagon
v.
Mound Case)
105. Compensation is to be assessed on the basis of:
(A) Rough estimate of loss generally resulting from death
(B) Approximate calculation of damage a result of death
as
(C) Legitimate expectation of loss of pecuniary benefits
(D) Closeness in relationship between claimants and the deceased
XXII. Ahmadi, J. (as he then was) speaking for himself and Punchhi, J., endorsed the
recommendations in the following words-The time is ripe for taking stock of the working of
the various Tribunals set up in the country after the insertion of Articles 323-A and 323-B
in the Constitution. After the incorporation of these two articles, Acts have been enacted
where-under tribunals have been constituted for dispensation of justice. Sufficient time has
passed and experience gained in these last few for taking stock of the situation with

constituted. Complaints have been heard in regard to the functioning of other tribunals
well and it is time that body like the Law Commission of India has comprehensive
